findings.title: Validator performs DB writes on every validation
findings.body: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb line 13, EmailValidator#validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value), and BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count, sets last_match_at and calls save. Validation is supposed to be side-effect free and can run multiple times per User save, on any attribute change that leaves email_changed? true, and even on valid? checks that never save. Consequence: match_count/last_match_at are inflated, extra SELECT+UPDATE on every signup/email-change validation, and a failed User save still commits BlockedEmail stats in a separate transaction.

findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates
findings.body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb lines 14-16, should_block? does record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save. This is read-modify-write with two separate queries. Concurrent blocked signup attempts for the same email will both read the same count and overwrite each other, losing counts. It also runs validations/callbacks and updates updated_at. Consequence: inaccurate blocking statistics under concurrency; should use atomic increment_counter / update_counters / update_columns.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
findings.body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb line 12, BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first does an exact case-sensitive match, and EmailValidator passes the raw value without downcasing/normalizing. User emails differ in case (e.g., BAD@spammers.org vs bad@spammers.org). Consequence: an attacker can bypass a blocked-email entry simply by changing letter case, and BlockedEmail uniqueness validation also permits duplicate entries differing only by case.

findings.title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored
findings.body: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb lines 18-22, the check builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) with no end-anchor and only escapes dots. An email like user@allowed.com.evil.com contains substring @allowed.com and will pass a whitelist for allowed.com, and similarly blacklist entries can be evaded with suffix subdomains. Consequence: domain restrictions moved from User to EmailValidator remain bypassable for both whitelist and blacklist.

findings.title: Wrong Ember dependent key for rejectedEmails
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js line 96, emailValidation declares .property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each') but rejectedEmails is an array of plain strings. @each observes properties of array items, not array membership; for primitive arrays the correct key is rejectedEmails.[] (or .length). Consequence: after createAccount pushes a server-rejected email via pushObject, emailValidation may not recompute, so the form still shows the blocked email as ok/submittable until the user edits the email field.

findings.title: Whitelist/blacklist branches have no coverage
findings.body: In spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb, the only tests stub BlockedEmail.should_block? true/false and assert presence of errors. There are no tests for email_domains_whitelist, email_domains_blacklist, the interaction where whitelist errors should suppress the blocked check, nil/malformed values, or real BlockedEmail integration. Consequence: regressions in the moved restriction logic from User#email_validator and the new blocked-email branch will not be caught.
